authority: read-only snapshot of existing manual source resolution; no new model assignment
source_query:
select m.id::text as source_template_id,
m.line_key,m.train_number,m.calendar_urn,m.railway_urn,m.direction_urn,
m.source_path,m.source_revision_date::text as source_revision_date,
cardinality(m.operating_dates) as explicit_date_count,
case when cardinality(m.operating_dates)>0 then min_date::text end as first_operating_date,
case when cardinality(m.operating_dates)>0 then max_date::text end as last_operating_date,
'2026-11-16'::date = any(m.operating_dates) as listed_on_2026_11_16,
s.mapping_level,s.vehicle_type,s.vehicle_artwork_path,
s.vehicle_source_url,s.vehicle_revision_date::text as vehicle_revision_date,
s.timetable_validity
from public.manual_timetable_templates m
join public.train_timetable_source_resolution s on s.source_template_id=m.id
cross join lateral (select min(d) as min_date,max(d) as max_date from unnest(m.operating_dates) d) days
where s.vehicle_artwork_path is not null order by m.line_key,m.train_number,m.id
interpretation: A dated_schedule_rule links a historical timetable source row and model PNG. This is NOT a claim it runs on current date; explicit operating_dates null means current operating date NOT verified. Never use as a global number band.
